# Fixture PDFs

`viewer.spec.ts` and the evaluation harness read their PDFs from this directory. They skip with a
named message while a file is missing, so the suite never reports success for a test it did not
run.

These files are not in the repository yet. They must be **fictional** documents, or documents
explicitly approved for sending to TypeSafe AI (spec §10).

## Present

| File                       | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bitcoin.pdf`              | The Bitcoin whitepaper, byte-identical to `assets/bitcoin.pdf`. Supplied, committed, and driven by `bitcoin.spec.ts`; `bitcoin-asset.spec.ts` drives the copy in `assets/` instead, so the document handed to a reader for a demonstration is the one the segmentation numbers are measured against. It is English, nine pages, and produced by a third-party toolchain, so it covers the paths the generated Japanese sample cannot: Latin word spacing, multi-page navigation, and a real producer's item splitting. `bitcoin.spec.ts` and `bitcoin-asset.spec.ts` intercept `/api/search`, so those suites send nothing. `npm run eval` **does** send it: the §11.1 set includes eighteen queries written against this paper by an outside reviewer, and the whitepaper is a public document, so it is an approved subject under spec §10. |
| `sample-contract-ja.pdf`   | Generated by `npm run fixtures:sample`; gitignored. See the repository README.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `sample-two-column-ja.pdf` | Generated by `npm run fixtures:sample`; gitignored. Two floated columns, so `limits.spec.ts` can check that a layout spec §2 does not claim to handle is named to the reader rather than silently trusted.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `eval-terms-ja.pdf`        | Generated by `npm run fixtures:sample`; gitignored. The subject of the §11.1 evaluation set and of nothing else — a fictional terms-of-service document deliberately **not** used to tune segmentation, thresholds or batching, because measuring quality on a document a rule was fitted to reports the fit rather than the quality. `npm run eval` reads it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `sample-near-limit-ja.pdf` | Generated by `npm run fixtures:sample`; gitignored. 48 pages and 1,872 segments — 94% of the segment cap — inside every declared limit, so it times a near-capacity search — the one number §6.4's deadline rests on that nothing else measures.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

## Required files

| File              | Purpose                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contract-ja.pdf` | Primary fixture for `viewer.spec.ts` and most evaluation cases |
| `terms-ja.pdf`    | Second document for the evaluation set                         |
| `policy-ja.pdf`   | Third document for the evaluation set                          |

## Required characteristics

Each PDF must be text based, horizontally written, single column, at most 50 pages and 10 MB, and
written in Japanese (spec §2).

`contract-ja.pdf` additionally needs:

- A clause stating that already-paid fees are not refunded on early termination, **without using
  the everyday word `返金`** — this is what spec §13's demonstration turns on, and what separates
  meaning search from exact search.
- A notice-period clause, for example "解約する場合は満了日の30日前までに書面で通知する".
- A prohibition on transferring the right to use the service to a third party.
- **A sentence that appears verbatim in two different places.** Spec §11.2 requires that selecting
  a result highlights the occurrence that result represents, and that cannot be tested without
  deliberately repeated text.

## Authoring the evaluation cases

`tests/evaluation-cases.json` currently carries the case schema and the worked examples from the
specification. The fixed 20-query set required by spec §11.1 must be authored against the real
fixtures once they exist, because an expectation can only name a passage the document contains.
Keep it separate from any threshold-tuning examples.

Expectations are matched by normalized text containment rather than by segment ID, so tuning the
segmentation does not silently invalidate or, worse, silently pass the frozen set.
